scope: Read-only inventory of zdp behaviour (Java paths are relative to /home/terryvanbelle/projects/vibe/bc26a0/java/bots/zdp/; other paths are relative to /home/terryvanbelle/projects/vibe/bc26a0/) that none of the 16 decision points (D.java:39-47, DK.java:16-19) controls. It covers the fixed turn skeletons and the gates that decide whether a point opens, zdb fallbacks, navigation, errand targets, combat, trap and cat code, economy and spawning, formation and rescue, comms, free pickups, and the Cfg constants behind each. It also lists how every point is gated, overridden or post-processed. Rates come from the cpi-x0 records: 256 self-play games mirroring rl-m2 v39, with floors 0.1 on king points, 0.05 on MINE_PICK and 0.03 on BABY_ROLE (configs/cpi-x0.json purpose). The files are /tmp/claude-1000/-home-terryvanbelle-projects-vibe-bc26a0/31310128-fb77-4058-8e53-1da41e55d47b/scratchpad/aspace/cpi-x0-summary.json and /tmp/claude-1000/-home-terryvanbelle-projects-vibe-bc26a0/31310128-fb77-4058-8e53-1da41e55d47b/scratchpad/aspace/devfb-cpi-x0.json. Nothing was edited, built or run apart from reading files and those JSON summaries. Bytecode limits are off in this work (docs/engine.md:17-21), so every clock gate below is inert.
strategy_summary:
zdb, as replayed by zdp, puts the economy first, backstabs at a fixed early round and insures the king count at the end of the game.
1. Kings: each king settles on the nearest known home-half mine within dist2 400 of its start and never re-picks it (King.java:386, 927-943). Every turn it picks up all piles under its 3x3 (King.java:43, 179-188). It stays put whenever an enemy or cat is visible (King.java:384), and at war it bites the weakest adjacent enemy (King.java:57, 190-264).
2. Spawning: a king always builds a core of 18 babies (12 on maps of 441 tiles or fewer) while cheese covers cost plus a floor. Beyond that it builds only if the projected end-of-game surplus covers cost + 100; the projection uses 75% of measured income minus 200 per king (King.java:285-316; Econ.java:18-41). Babies are capped at 18 (40 with 1000 banked, 80 with 3000; King.java:267-271).
3. Roles at birth: the first 6 babies gather; later ones alternate gatherer and cat-fighter by round parity. Babies 4-15 born before round 300 are attackers that rush the mirrored enemy start. One in four gatherers scouts its own half until round 150 (Baby.java:318-342, 1189-1243, 1807-1809).
4. Gathering: gatherers spread over home-half mines, sorted by distance from home and offset by a per-rat slot (Baby.java:1473-1501). They wander the mine's 5x5 and chase visible piles. They deliver everything to the nearest king at 30 raw, at 10 when idle, and at any amount after round 1960 (Baby.java:1006, 1044, 1144-1157, 879-899). When a mine is crowded or idle they seek another (Baby.java:1830-1883).
5. War: from round 30 every baby is hostile, which ends cooperation (Baby.java:239-242; Cfg.java:146-148). Bites go to the king first, then the lowest-HP rat, with cheese added when that makes a kill. Babies grab weaker rats and throw them using a damage table (Baby.java:519-790). war() keeps gatherers defensive while fighters engage, and everyone answers a king's ALERT within dist2 225 (Baby.java:1245-1301).
6. Cats: gatherers flee within 20, fighters bite cats and defend kings, and cat traps go ahead of cats and, during cooperation, on cat lanes. From round 1850 at war every baby hunts cats for damage points (Baby.java:821-871, 1008-1016, 1405-1471).
7. King count: from round 80 (300 at war), the slot-0 king opens a second-king site once there are 16+ babies, 300 cheese and enough income (King.java:669-772). Two endgame paths (END_KING 1850, CASH_END 1880) aim to have 2 kings alive at round 2000, because kings weigh 0.5 of the war points (King.java:764-767; Baby.java:1579-1712; Cfg.java:75, 244).
8. Comms: kings own the 64-slot array (kings, symmetry, alerts, mines, cats, budget, formation), and babies squeak news to the kings (Comms.java:10-22; Baby.java:903-932; King.java:131-176).
9. Movement: greedy steps, then a bug walk, then reverse-A* flow fields, with automatic digging; macro steps strafe to face enemies in range (Nav.java:72-210; Flow.java).

most_constraining: 1. Frozen baby points. This is a config choice, but it acts like hard-coding. rl-m2 and cpi-x0 train only points 5, 7, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 16 (configs/rl-m2.json:26-34; cpi-x0-summary.json 'trainable'). BABY_MOVE, ACT_PRE/POST, FACE, COMMS, FREE, BABY_VAL and the king's COMMS/VAL points stay at the imitation net; phase-B unlocks are planned as [[2,3,4],[6],[1]] (configs/rl-m2.json:35). So for RL every baby tactic in this inventory is fixed: errands, fights, throws, traps, delivery, cat responses and the round-30 backstab. BABY_MOVE's imitation pick reproduces zdb with p_top_mean 0.993 (devfb-cpi-x0.json point 1).

2. Silent fallback with loose masks, and fallback rows trained as if the option had run (Baby.java:2203-2206; DK.java:345-346; King.java:57, 74, 79, 309-316; scripts/rl_train.py:525-541). KING_ACT options 0..10 are always allowed (DK.java:594), KING_SPAWN has a null mask (DK.java:454), and KING_MOVE's mask is static (DK.java:350-355). Many floor-sampled deviations therefore change nothing yet are still credited: KING_ACT options 1-4/7-10 fall back 0.83-1.00, KING_MOVE 0.175 overall, KING_SPAWN builds 0.40-0.56.

3. A fixed king anchor. homeMine is chosen once and never re-picked (King.java:386, 927-943; DK.java:439-442), and every KING_MOVE macro option walks or digs back to it. 57.8% of KING_MOVE picks are stay-type.

4. The baby cap and spawn gates in zdb's spawn path (King.java:267-316): an 18-baby cap and the floors behind the hold labels, which are 88.5% of KING_SPAWN picks. Net builds bypass them only when the chosen ring tile is free and affordable.
5. The round-30 backstab in hostile() (Baby.java:239-242; Cfg.java:146-148). The frozen ACT imitation net and the ACT fallback both carry it, so RL cannot choose when cooperation ends.

6. No destination choice. Nav.goTo/Flow is the only multi-turn movement, and zdb picks the errand targets: home frame, firstSym, nearest king, mirrored enemy start (Nav.java:72-105; Baby.java:1144-1157, 1189-1243, 1719-1828). This becomes the dominant limit once BABY_MOVE is unfrozen.
7. MINE_PICK is limited to home-half mines whenever any exist, and is re-asked only at zdb's triggers (Baby.java:1481-1501, 1122-1141). 10.5% of its rows have a single candidate.

8. BABY_ROLE's cadence and fixed meaning. In RL it is reviewed every 50 rounds at a 0.001 floor (Cfg.java:260-262; configs/rl-m2.json floor_points), and zdb's cascade decides what each role does (Baby.java:1008-1100).
9. The economy signal. The king writes Econ.surplus to BUDGET every turn (Econ.java:18-41; King.java:83), and KING_COMMS can only set it to 0, 100 or 1023 and is frozen anyway (DK.java:55).
10. Formation: only the slot-0 king decides, zdb gates the king side, and baby joining and promotion are fixed (King.java:669-772; Baby.java:180-185, 1528-1559).
overrides: All points: when an option's executor returns false, zdb's code for that phase runs: BABY_MOVE falls to moveDecision (Baby.java:2203-2206), ACT_PRE/POST to zdb's blocks (Baby.java:130-145, 209-226), FACE to guardTurn (Baby.java:232-233), COMMS to zdb's held squeak (Baby.java:162-166), and the king points likewise (DK.java:345-346; King.java:74, 79, 309-316). The RL row still records the sampled k (D.java:158-162; scripts/rl_train.py:525-541).

KING_ACT: unless the net picked A_NONE (DK.java:490-506 hold flag), zdb's bite runs after the net's option, at war only (King.java:57). The ALERT write follows regardless (King.java:58-69). Options 0..10 are always allowed and only the 6 cheese-boosted bites are masked by applicability (DK.java:592-597). In cpi-x0, A_NONE is 90.2% of picks, options 1-4 and 7-10 fall back 83-100% of the time, and only A_TRAP_FORT (0.14) and A_MOAT_FILL (0.11) usually act.

KING_MOVE: eight options are the same 'stay': K_THREAT_HOLD, K_NO_HOME, K_AT_HOME, K_DIG_WAIT, K_DIG_POOR, K_STUCK, K_DIG_REFUSED and K_STAY (DK.java:418-420). K_LANE, K_NO_MINE, K_OFF_SITE and K_PATH are statically masked (DK.java:350-355). K_WALK_HOME, K_SIDESTEP and K_DIG target the fixed home() (DK.java:405-416, 439-442). closer() and step() refuse steps that split the ring (King.java:582-618, 653-663), which is why K_CLOSER falls back 0.77. Executor steps also call King.pickUp (DK.java:408, 427). The point opens only when movement-ready (King.java:77).

KING_SPAWN: null mask (DK.java:454). S_NO_SURPLUS, S_FLOOR, S_CAP, S_BLOCKED and S_HOLD are the same 'don't build'; only spawnWhy differs (DK.java:466-468, 477-478). S_DIG digs the ring toward the first enemy or the map centre and fails if nothing was dug (DK.java:469-476; fallback 0.85). S_BUILD_0..15 bypass the floors and the cap (DK.java:479-486), but a blocked or unaffordable tile falls back to zdb's gated spawn (King.java:309-316). The point opens only when action-ready (King.java:289).

KING_FORM: only the slot-0 king decides (King.java:72, 670). F_WAR_OFF, F_CAP_OFF and F_CAP_GAP all close the site (DK.java:646). F_DROP_FORMED and F_DROP_TIMEOUT close it if one is open (DK.java:655). F_END_WAIT, F_END_NONE, F_IDLE, F_NO_INCOME and F_NO_SITE are no-ops that succeed only when no site is open (DK.java:660-661). Start options are masked while a site is open or the king slots are full (DK.java:636-639).
KING_TURN: opens only when the king is turning-ready, action-ready and holds at least the rat cost (King.java:46). KT_ZDB keeps the current facing.

KING_COMMS: KC_ZDB keeps zdb's writes for the whole turn. The edits are limited to dropping write groups, three BUDGET bands {0, 100, 1023}, ALERT call/clear, a squeak, trap removal and KC_SET writes (DK.java:49-59). zdb rewrites BUDGET (King.java:83) and ALERT (King.java:58-69) every turn before this point. Frozen in RL; KC_ZDB is 99.5% of picks.

BABY_ACT_PRE: A_PASS counts as acted (Baby.java:1923), so it also suppresses the hard-coded cash and formation promotions for that turn (Baby.java:174-185). A_THROW runs tryThrow and fails under THROW_HOLD (Baby.java:1934-1938, 694), giving fallback 0.97. Options 0..20 are always allowed (Baby.java:2056-2057). If an option promotes the rat to king, the turn ends (Baby.java:127).

BABY_ACT_POST: opens only if the rat is still action-ready after the move (Baby.java:200), and macro digs use up that readiness. If its option fails, zdb's post block runs: drop or throw, carry, bites, cat bite, layLane in cooperation, tryDeliver (Baby.java:209-226).

BABY_MOVE: macro options keep zdb's internals (targets, Nav digs, guard facing, dropping the target on stall). M_GRAB, M_RESCUE, M_HUNGRY, M_ATK_DELIVER and M_FORT are always masked (Baby.java:2258, 2264, 2267, 2275, 2279). Some options duplicate each other: M_RAID and M_RAID_FIGHT (Baby.java:2346-2349); M_COURIER and M_SCOUT_HOME (Baby.java:2383-2405); M_CAT_DEFEND and M_FIGHT_CAT, both approachCat (Baby.java:2313-2315, 2375-2378); P_STEP and P_RISK share an executor and have complementary masks (Baby.java:2300, 2303, 2444-2453). netBook runs zdb's attacker bookkeeping every turn before the pick (Baby.java:2213-2221). Primitive steps leave Nav.stall unchanged (Baby.java:2451-2452).
BABY_FACE: opens only when turning-ready (Baby.java:229), which a turning step has usually used up. A failed option runs guardTurn (Baby.java:232-233).
BABY_COMMS: zdb's cashTick and report() still run, muted, and update zdb's state. If the net's option cannot squeak, zdb's held squeak goes out instead (Baby.java:150-166).

MINE_PICK: opens only inside zdb's pickMine calls (fresh or reset, IDLE_SHIFT, retry; D.java:120-121). The pick is dropped when the mine list changes or the walk stalls (Baby.java:1122-1141). Candidates are home-half mines whenever any exist (Baby.java:1481-1483, 1496).

BABY_ROLE: reviewed only at birth, after a change, or every DP_ROLE_EVERY rounds (Baby.java:41-49, 86-91). roleExec resets errand state on a real change (Baby.java:1894-1907). The scout and raider bits change only the fallback's behaviour (Baby.java:1027-1028, 1062, 1807-1809), because net M_RAID/M_SCOUT ignore them (Baby.java:2270, 2288).

BABY_FREE: FR_ZDB runs zdb's pickUp. A cap or none choice holds for the whole turn, including a later pickAdjacent (Baby.java:40, 420, 1104-1112). Trap removals chain up to FREE_CHAIN 2 (Baby.java:453-462; D.java:106). Phase 0 gives attackers no pickup (Baby.java:465).
cross_cutting: Duplicate options dilute the uniform floor and split probability and credit among identical actions. KING_SPAWN has 5 identical holds among 22 options (DK.java:466-468, 477-478). KING_MOVE has 8 identical stays among 33 allowed options (DK.java:418-420). KING_FORM has 3 identical close options plus 5 no-ops (DK.java:646, 660-661). BABY_MOVE has M_RAID/M_RAID_FIGHT, M_COURIER/M_SCOUT_HOME, M_CAT_DEFEND/M_FIGHT_CAT and P_STEP/P_RISK. The floor is spread uniformly over allowed options (D.java:30-31; DNet.java:30-31), so in cpi-x0 'stay' gets 8/33 of KING_MOVE's 0.1 floor.

Most trainable options are zdb's exit reasons (S_CAP, K_AT_HOME, F_CAP_OFF), not distinct actions, so each point has fewer real choices than options. KING_SPAWN: hold, dig the ring, or build at ring tile i. KING_MOVE: stay, flee or dodge, walk or dig toward home, walk to a pile, or step or dig in direction d. KING_FORM: close, hold, rich drop or gap, or open a site of some kind or ring offset. KING_ACT: no bite, a zdb-bite variant, traps, moat fill, dig the ring, or a cheese-boosted bite (DK.java:25-47).

The imitation start is saturated. Share of rows where the top pick is saturated, per cpi-x0-summary.json: BABY_MOVE 0.79, ACT_PRE 0.90, ACT_POST 0.99, ROLE 0.95, KING_SPAWN 0.75, KING_ACT 0.76, KING_FORM 0.71, MINE_PICK 0.64, KING_MOVE 0.35. Deviations therefore come almost entirely from the floors.

Most trainable king decisions are 'do nothing', and the hard-coded gates above decide when that is right. In cpi-x0: KING_MOVE 57.8% stay-type; KING_SPAWN 88.5% hold; KING_ACT 90.2% A_NONE; KING_FORM 84.7% close or idle (F_CAP_OFF 43.1%, F_IDLE 22.5%, F_WAR_OFF 19.1%).

Bytecode limits are off (docs/engine.md:17-21; scripts/es_eval.sh:7). Every clock gate is inert and Flow searches finish within the turn. Self-play results may not carry over to tournament limits, where BC_BAIL (Baby.java:112) would skip whole baby turns.

zdb's bookkeeping also runs on net turns: netBook (Baby.java:2213-2221), the muted cashTick and report() (Baby.java:150-166), the Econ ring and the Comms reads. That keeps zdb's state consistent so the fallback can take over at any moment. As a result, even unfrozen points act like a net layered over a live zdb policy, not a free controller.
